messages.text: Make sure the radius of the revised file is still within bounds for the cables and services - remove the outermost row if needed
I’ll check the revised module bodies against the cable and service envelope. If the outer ring exceeds it, I’ll remove that ring, recheck coverage and overlap, and update PR41.

The revised outer ring reaches 202.0 mm, beyond the 188.5 mm local-support radius and into the service reservation that starts at 190 mm. I’ll remove that ring and measure the remaining clearance. I’ll also report the resulting coverage loss.

The ACTS preflight reports changed setup fingerprints, so I’m rechecking the installed runtime with the acts-spack workflow. I’ll keep the service boundaries fixed and validate the trimmed layout against them.

Removing the outer ring leaves 296 modules in eight rings. Their maximum occupied radius is 183.39 mm, giving 5.11 mm clearance to the plate edge and 6.61 mm to the 190 mm service boundary. This leaves roughly 2.5–3.3% of the original annulus uncovered in the sampled projections; I’ll retain that loss in the report and checks.

The geometry and service-bound checks pass. The native ACTS audit is running with added outer-edge tracks to check the coverage loss. The fixed trunk and flange-neck calculations still show cable-packing failures; removing the ring restores radial clearance but does not resolve those capacity limits.

ACTS agrees with the analytic intersections for all 378 tracks per layout. All 54 added edge probes miss the trimmed disc, confirming the coverage loss. I’m retaining those results and updating PR41’s figures, description and validation evidence.

The trimmed layout is pushed to [PR41](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/41), and hosted validation is starting.

The previous radial turn’s resource log is also published: 8,196,394 input tokens, including 7,991,552 cached; 66,397 output tokens, including 31,626 reasoning; 8,262,791 total. This service-radius turn has a separate log.

Hosted validation has passed the project-record checks and is running the geometry controls. The published layout stays within the fixed radial bounds; the report retains the outer-edge coverage loss and cable-packing failures.

Hosted geometry and export checks have passed, including the new disc controls. The remaining checks are the dashboard and documentation links. PR41’s current report records the clearance, overlap and coverage-loss figures.
The final hosted build passed. PR41 is complete with the eight-ring layout and its coverage and packing limitations recorded. I’m scheduling one-time usage recovery for this turn after it closes.

Updated [PR41](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/41): removed the outer **63-module ring**, leaving **296 modules in eight rings**.

Maximum occupied radius is **183.39 mm**, providing:

- **6.61 mm** clearance to the 190 mm service boundary.
